title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Summary of the National Symposium on Adjudicating Economic Crime Cases
keywords_en: corruption; trial of economic crime cases by courts nationwide
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the Summary of the National Courts Symposium on Handling Economic Crime Cases

Fa [2003] No. 167

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Summary of the National Courts Symposium on Handling Economic Crime Cases is hereby issued for your reference in implementation. Please promptly report any issues encountered during implementation to this Court.

November 13, 2003

Summary of the National Courts Symposium on Handling Economic Crime Cases

To further strengthen the work of the People's Courts in adjudicating economic crime cases, the Supreme People's Court convened the National Courts Symposium on Handling Economic Crime Cases in Chongqing from June 4 to 6, 2002. The symposium was attended by the vice presidents in charge of criminal adjudication and the chiefs of criminal divisions of the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army. The Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security were also invited to send representatives to participate. The symposium summarized the work and experience of the People's Courts in adjudicating economic crime cases since the revision and implementation of the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law, analyzed the situation and tasks faced in handling such cases, and made arrangements to further strengthen the work of the People's Courts in adjudicating economic crime cases for the current and future periods. The symposium focused on discussing several issues concerning the application of law encountered by the People's Courts in adjudicating cases of embezzlement, bribery, and dereliction of duty, and reached a consensus on some of the common issues. After collation and solicitation of opinions from relevant departments, the summary is as follows:

I. Regarding the Subjects of Crimes of Embezzlement, Bribery, and Dereliction of Duty

(1) Determination of State Organ Staff

The term "state organ staff" as used in the Criminal Law refers to persons who engage in public service within a state organ, including those who engage in public service in state organs at all levels, such as the organs of state power, administrative organs, judicial organs, and military organs.

According to the relevant legislative interpretation, persons who engage in public service in organizations that exercise state administrative powers in accordance with laws and regulations, or in organizations entrusted by state organs to exercise state powers on their behalf, or persons who, although not included in the staffing of state organs, engage in public service within state organs, are regarded as state organ staff. In judicial practice, persons who engage in public service in the organs of the Communist Party of China at the township (town) level or above, or in the organs of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, shall also be regarded as state organ staff.

(2) Determination of Persons Dispatched by State Organs, State-owned Companies, Enterprises, or Institutions to Engage in Public Service in Non-State-owned Companies, Enterprises, Institutions, or Social Organizations

The term "dispatch" means appointment or delegation, and its forms are diverse, such as appointment, assignment, nomination, approval, etc. Regardless of the identity of the dispatched person, as long as they accept dispatch from a state organ, state-owned company, enterprise, or institution, and represent the state organ, state-owned company, enterprise, or institution in engaging in organizational, leadership, supervisory, or management work in non-state-owned companies, enterprises, institutions, or social organizations, they can be determined as persons dispatched by a state organ, state-owned company, enterprise, or institution to engage in public service in non-state-owned companies, enterprises, institutions, or social organizations. For example, persons dispatched by state organs, state-owned companies, enterprises, or institutions to engage in organizational, leadership, supervisory, or management work in state-controlled or state-invested joint-stock companies shall be regarded as state functionaries. After a state-owned company or enterprise is restructured into a joint-stock company, among the original staff of the state-owned company or enterprise and newly appointed personnel of the joint-stock company, except those who exercise supervisory or management authority on behalf of the state investment entity, others shall not be regarded as state functionaries.

(3) Determination of "Other Persons Who Engage in Public Service According to Law"

The "other persons who engage in public service according to law" as provided in Article 93, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law shall have two characteristics: first, they exercise state management functions under specific conditions; second, they engage in public service according to law. This specifically includes: (1) deputies to People's Congresses at all levels who perform their duties according to law; (2) people's jurors who perform judicial duties according to law; (3) personnel of grassroots organizations in rural and urban areas, such as villagers' committees and residents' committees, who assist township people's governments or subdistrict offices in administrative management; and (4) other persons authorized by law to engage in public service.

(4) Understanding of "Engaging in Public Service"

Engaging in public service means performing duties such as organization, leadership, supervision, and management on behalf of state organs, state-owned companies, enterprises, institutions, or people's organizations. Public service is mainly manifested in public affairs related to official authority and the official activities of supervising and managing state-owned property. For example, state organ staff performing duties according to law, and directors, managers, supervisors, accountants, cashiers, etc., of state-owned companies managing and supervising state-owned property, constitute engaging in public service. Those labor services or technical service work that do not involve official authority, such as the work performed by salesclerks or ticket sellers, are generally not considered public service.

II. Regarding the Crime of Embezzlement

(1) Determination of Completion and Attempt of the Crime of Embezzlement

The crime of embezzlement is a property-related duty crime aimed at illegal possession. Similar to property crimes such as theft, fraud, and robbery, the standard for distinguishing between completion and attempt of the crime of embezzlement should be whether the actor has actually taken control of the property. If the actor, by taking advantage of their official position, has carried out embezzlement acts such as falsely balancing accounts, but the public property has not actually been transferred, or has been discovered before being taken control of by the actor, it shall be found to be an attempted embezzlement. After the actor takes control of the public property, whether they convert the property to their own possession does not affect the finding of a completed embezzlement.

(2) Determination of "Being Entrusted to Manage or Operate State-owned Property"

The phrase "being entrusted to manage or operate state-owned property" as provided in Article 382, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law refers to managing or operating state-owned property due to contracting, leasing, temporary employment, etc.

(3) Determination of Acts of State Functionaries and Non-State Functionaries Colluding to Unlawfully Possess Unit Property Together

For acts where a state functionary colludes with others to unlawfully possess unit property together, punishment shall be determined and imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Joint Crimes in Embezzlement and Job-occupancy Crimes. Where, in a company, enterprise, or other unit, a non-state functionary and a state functionary collude, each taking advantage of their respective official positions, to jointly unlawfully possess the property of the unit, an effort should be made to distinguish between the principal and accessory offenders, and the nature of the crime shall be determined according to the principal offender. In judicial practice, if, based on the actual circumstances of the case, the status and role of each joint offender in the joint crime are comparable and it is difficult to distinguish between principal and accessory offenders, the crime may be punished as embezzlement.

(4) Determination of "Individual Embezzlement Amount" in Joint Embezzlement Crimes

The "individual embezzlement amount" as provided in Article 383, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law shall, in cases of joint embezzlement crimes, be understood as the amount of embezzlement in which the individual participated or which they organized or directed, and shall not be determined solely by the amount of stolen money actually divided by the individual. For an accessory in a joint embezzlement crime, the sentencing range shall be determined based on the amount of joint embezzlement in which they participated, and they shall be given a lighter, mitigated, or exempted punishment in accordance with Article 27, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law.

III. Regarding the Crime of Bribery

(1) Determination of "Taking Advantage of One's Official Position"

The phrase "taking advantage of one's official position" as provided in Article 385, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law includes not only the use of one's own authority to supervise, be responsible for, or handle a certain public affair, but also the use of the authority of other state functionaries who are subordinate to or constrained by one's own position. If a state functionary holding a leadership position in a unit uses the official position of a state functionary in a subordinate department not directly under their supervision to seek benefits for others, this shall be found to constitute "taking advantage of one's official position" to seek benefits for others.

(2) Determination of "Seeking Benefits for Others"

Seeking benefits for others includes three phases: promising, implementing, and achieving benefits. As long as the actor's conduct involves any one of these phases, such as a state functionary, upon receiving property from others and in response to a specific request made by the other party, promising to seek benefits for them, the element of seeking benefits for others is established. If the state functionary is aware that the other party has a specific request and still accepts property from them, this is deemed a promise to seek benefits for the other party.

(3) Determination of "Taking Advantage of the Convenient Conditions Formed by One's Authority or Position"

The phrase "taking advantage of the convenient conditions formed by one's own authority or position" as provided in Article 388 of the Criminal Law means that although there is no subordinate or constraining relationship in terms of official positions between the actor and the state functionary being used, the actor has taken advantage of the influence generated by their own authority or position and certain work connections, such as between state functionaries in different departments within the same unit, between state functionaries in superior and subordinate units without a subordinate or constraining official relationship, or between state functionaries of different units who have work connections.

(4) Handling of Acts of Former State Functionaries Accepting Property

Referring to the spirit of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Handle Acts of State Functionaries Who, by Taking Advantage of Their Official Positions to Seek Benefits for Others, Accept Property After Retirement, if a state functionary, by taking advantage of their official position, seeks benefits for a petitioner and, with prior agreement with the petitioner, accepts property from the petitioner after leaving office, and such conduct constitutes a crime, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of bribery.

(5) Determination of Joint Bribery Crimes

According to the provisions of the Criminal Law on joint crimes, if a non-state functionary colludes with a state functionary and jointly engages in bribery, they shall be investigated for criminal liability as an accomplice in the crime of bribery. Whether a non-state functionary constitutes an accomplice in the crime of bribery depends on whether there is a common intent and conduct for bribery between the parties. If a close relative of a state functionary conveys a request to the state functionary on behalf of the petitioner, accepts property from the petitioner and informs the state functionary, or if a state functionary, knowing that their close relative has accepted property from another person, still uses their official position to seek benefits for that person as requested by the close relative, the state functionary shall be found to have committed the crime of bribery, and the close relative shall be dealt with as an accomplice in the crime of bribery. If a person other than a close relative conspires with a state functionary to seek benefits for a petitioner by taking advantage of the state functionary's official position, and they jointly possess the property accepted from the petitioner after receiving it, they constitute an accomplice in the crime of bribery. If a state functionary, by taking advantage of their official position, seeks benefits for others and instructs others to deliver property to a third party, and such conduct constitutes a crime, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of bribery.

(6) Determination of Acts of Demanding or Illegally Accepting Property in the Name of a Loan

If a state functionary, by taking advantage of their official position, demands property from others in the name of a loan, or illegally accepts property to seek benefits for others, this shall be found to constitute bribery. In making the specific determination, one cannot simply look at whether there is a written loan agreement; a comprehensive assessment shall be made based on the following factors: (1) whether there is a legitimate and reasonable reason for the loan; (2) the destination of the funds; (3) the usual relationship between the parties and whether there have been financial dealings; (4) whether the lender has asked the state functionary to use their official position to seek benefits for them; (5) whether there was an expression or act of repayment after the loan; (6) whether there was the ability to repay; (7) the reason for non-repayment; etc.

(7) Determination of Bribery Cases Involving Stocks

When handling bribery cases involving stocks, attention should be paid to the following: (1) If a state functionary, by taking advantage of their official position, demands or illegally accepts stocks without paying the share capital, and seeks benefits for others, thereby constituting the crime of bribery, the bribery amount shall be calculated based on the actual price of the stocks at the time of acceptance. (2) If the actor pays the share capital to purchase stocks that are likely to appreciate in value, since this does not constitute gratuitous acceptance of property from the petitioner, it shall not be punished as the crime of bribery. (3) If the stocks have already been listed and appreciated in value, and the actor only pays the share capital, the difference between the actual price of the stocks at the time of "purchase" and the share capital shall be found to constitute bribery.

IV. Regarding the Crime of Misappropriation of Public Funds

(1) Determination of Acts Where a Unit Decides to Lend Public Funds to Individuals

If, after collective discussion by the unit's leadership, a decision is made to lend public funds to individuals, or if the person in charge of the unit decides to lend public funds to individuals for the benefit of the unit, the act shall not be punished as the crime of misappropriation of public funds. If the above acts cause significant losses to the unit and constitute another crime, the responsible persons shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law.

(2) Determination of Acts of Misappropriating Public Funds for Use by Other Units

According to the Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 384, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, making public funds available for use by other units in a personal name or an individual's decision to make public funds available for use by other units in the name of the unit for personal gain shall be deemed as misappropriation of public funds for personal use. In judicial practice, when determining whether making public funds available for use by other units constitutes using a personal name, one should not merely look at the form but grasp the essence. If the actor evades financial supervision, or agrees with the user to conduct the transaction in a personal name, or both the borrowing and repayment are conducted in a personal name, and public funds are made available to other units, it shall be found to be in a personal name. An individual's decision includes decisions made within the scope of authority as well as decisions exceeding the scope of authority. Seeking personal gain includes both situations where the actor has agreed with the user in advance to seek personal gain but has not yet obtained it, and situations where personal gain has actually been obtained even without prior agreement. The personal gain includes both illegitimate benefits and legitimate benefits; it includes both property benefits and non-property benefits, provided that such non-property benefits are specific and actual interests, such as enrollment in school or employment.

(3) Determination of Acts Where a Leader of a State-owned Unit Borrows Public Funds from a Subordinate Unit with Legal Person Status Under Their Supervision for Personal Use

If a leader of a state-owned unit, by taking advantage of their official position, instructs a subordinate unit with legal person status to make public funds available for personal use, this constitutes an act of misappropriation of public funds. If the act constitutes a crime, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of misappropriation of public funds.

(4) Determination of the Nature of Acts of Pledging Negotiable Securities or Financial Instruments

If financial instruments or negotiable securities are misappropriated for use as a pledge, thereby placing public funds at risk, which is essentially no different from misappropriating public funds to provide a guarantee for others, and the requirements of the Criminal Law concerning the crime of misappropriation of public funds are met, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of misappropriation of public funds. The amount of misappropriated public funds shall be determined based on the amount of risk actually or potentially borne.

(5) Determination of the Nature of Acts of Misappropriating Public Funds to Repay Personal Debts

If public funds are misappropriated to repay personal debts, the specific type of misappropriation of public funds shall be determined based on the reason for the debt. Repayment of personal debts arising from illegal activities or profit-making activities shall be deemed as misappropriation of public funds for illegal activities or profit-making activities.

(6) Determination of the Nature of Acts of Misappropriating Public Funds for Registering a Company or Enterprise

Applying for registered capital is a preparation for production and business activities and is part of the profit-making activities of establishing a company or enterprise. Therefore, misappropriating public funds to be used by individuals for the verification of registered capital of a company or enterprise shall be deemed as misappropriation of public funds for profit-making activities.

(7) Determination of the Nature of Acts Where Public Funds Are Misappropriated but Not Yet Put to Actual Use

If public funds are misappropriated but not yet put to actual use, as long as the elements of a relatively large amount and failure to repay for more than three months are both present, the act shall be found to constitute the crime of misappropriation of public funds, but a lighter punishment may be given as appropriate.

(8) Determination of the Conversion of Misappropriation of Public Funds into Embezzlement

The main difference between the crime of misappropriation of public funds and the crime of embezzlement lies in whether the actor subjectively has the intent to unlawfully possess the public funds. Whether misappropriation of public funds is converted into embezzlement shall be determined and found by specifically judging whether the actor subjectively has the intent to unlawfully possess the public funds, in accordance with the principle of unity of subjectivity and objectivity. In judicial practice, where any of the following circumstances exists, the actor may be found to have the intent to unlawfully possess public funds:

1. According to the provisions of Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Misappropriation of Public Funds, if the actor absconds with the misappropriated public funds, the portion of the misappropriated public funds that was taken shall be convicted and punished as the crime of embezzlement.

2. If, after misappropriating public funds, the actor uses methods such as falsifying invoices to balance accounts or destroying relevant account books, making it difficult for the misappropriated public funds to be reflected in the unit's financial accounts, and there is no act of repayment, the actor shall be convicted and punished for the crime of embezzlement.

3. If the actor intercepts unit income without recording it, unlawfully possesses it, making the possessed public funds difficult to reflect in the unit's financial accounts, and there is no act of repayment, the actor shall be convicted and punished for the crime of embezzlement.

4. If there is evidence proving that the actor has the ability to repay the misappropriated public funds but refuses to do so and conceals the whereabouts of the misappropriated public funds, the actor shall be convicted and punished for the crime of embezzlement.

V. Regarding the Crime of Holding a Huge Amount of Property with Unexplained Sources

(1) Determination of the Actor's Inability to Explain the Legitimate Source of a Huge Amount of Property

The phrase cannot explain as provided in Article 395, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law includes the following situations: (1) the actor refuses to explain the source of the property; (2) the actor is unable to explain the specific source of the property; (3) the source of property stated by the actor is verified by the judicial authorities to be untrue; (4) the source of property stated by the actor cannot be verified by the judicial authorities due to reasons such as insufficiently specific clues, but it can be ruled out that there is a possibility and reasonableness of a legitimate source.

(2) Calculation of the Amount of Illegal Income

The "illegal income" as provided in Article 395 of the Criminal Law generally refers to the total of all the actor's property and all identifiable expenditures minus the income that can be proven to have a legitimate source. In the specific calculation, attention should be paid to the following issues: (1) The personal property of the state functionary and the property and expenditures of family members living with them should be calculated together, and all their legitimate income and the illegal income of family members living with them that is indeed personal should be subtracted together. (2) The property owned by the actor includes real property and movable property such as houses, furniture, daily necessities, school supplies, stocks, bonds, and deposits; the expenditures of the actor include legitimate and illegitimate expenditures, including daily living, work, and study expenses, fines, and property used for bribing others; the legitimate income of the actor includes various incomes allowed by law and policy, such as wages, bonuses, remuneration for writing, and inheritance. (3) To facilitate the calculation of the amount of the crime, the property and legitimate income of the actor may generally be calculated from the time when the actor has a relatively definite income and property.

VI. Regarding the Crime of Dereliction of Duty

(1) Determination of Significant Losses to Public Property Caused by Acts of Dereliction of Duty

According to the provisions of the Criminal Law, crimes of dereliction of duty, including negligent dereliction of duty and abuse of power, require as a constitutive element the causing of substantial losses to public property, the state, and the interests of the people. Among these, substantial losses to public property generally refer to major economic losses already caused by the dereliction of duty. In judicial practice, where any of the following circumstances exists, even though public property exists as a credit right, if such credit right can no longer be realized, it may be deemed that the perpetrator's dereliction of duty caused economic losses: (1) the debtor has been declared bankrupt through legal proceedings; (2) the debtor has absconded and his whereabouts are unknown; (3) due to the perpetrator's fault, the statute of limitations has expired; (4) other circumstances where there is evidence that the credit right cannot be realized.

(2) Statute of Limitations for the Crime of Negligent Dereliction of Duty

Where the substantial loss caused by the act of negligent dereliction of duty did not occur at the time of the act but occurred at a later time, the limitation period for prosecution of the crime of negligent dereliction of duty shall be calculated from the date on which the harmful result occurred.

(3) Application of Law to Crimes of Dereliction of Duty by Personnel of State-owned Companies and Enterprises

For acts of dereliction of duty (excluding acts of engaging in malpractices for personal gain) committed by personnel of state-owned companies and enterprises prior to the implementation of the Amendment to the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China on December 24, 1999, which have not yet been handled or are being handled, criminal liability cannot be pursued under the Criminal Law Amendment.

(4) Understanding of "Engaging in Malpractices for Personal Gain"

The term "engaging in malpractices for personal gain" in the crime of dereliction of duty involving malpractices shall be understood as seeking personal favor or personal gain. Where a state organ staff member commits acts of abuse of power or negligent dereliction of duty for the benefit of their own unit, constituting a crime, they shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 397, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law.
